issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of known answers. The change only adds a warm-start SLSQP stage. The new objective is -sum(r) plus a quadratic penalty that pulls each radius toward 0.1 (lam=2.0). Its result is then passed to the original SLSQP run as the starting point.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The objective and gradient match: d/dr of 0.5*lam*(r-rbar)^2 is lam*(r-rbar). The same constraints and bounds are used. If the first stage returns non-finite values, the code falls back to z0. The returned packing is still checked by the harness, so stage 1 cannot produce an invalid answer.

The numbers support the reject decision. The candidate's loss of -2.631 is about 0.005 worse than the incumbent's -2.6360, so lower is not achieved. A cost to note is that stage 1 adds up to 100 SLSQP iterations per start, which uses more of the time budget.

z cannot be recomputed from the data given. Each side has only one run, so there is no variance estimate. The reported z = -3543.18 implies a noise sigma of about 0.005/3543 ≈ 1.4e-6. That matches the stated run-to-run noise of about 1e-6, so the size of the reported z is plausible but cannot be checked. The candidate value is also rounded to 3 decimals, which limits precision.
